source_text: This view posits that even low complication rates (e.g., 0.2-0.6% for bleeding or infection in clinical settings) represent avoidable harm when alternatives like hygiene suffice, though rebuttals point to meta-analyses indicating net preventive gains that proxy decisions can reasonably approximate for minors unable to foresee long-term risks. [84]
